subject: chemistry
title: Conservation of Mass
welcome_lead: Atoms do not vanish. The mass before equals the mass after, every single time.
meta_desc: Learn the conservation of mass in this KS3 chemistry adventure on chemical reactions.
final_note: You now know the most important rule in chemistry: nothing disappears.

concepts.def: Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products.
Atoms swap partners but none are made or destroyed.
Sealed container where mass cannot escape.
Mass can leave (e.g. as gas) and seem to disappear.
Amount of matter, measured in grams (g) or kg.
Equipment used to measure mass accurately.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In every chemical reaction, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

Atoms cannot be created or destroyed.

walkthroughs.h2: Why does mass stay the same?
walkthroughs.body_html: The atoms simply rearrange into new combinations. If you start with 10 g of stuff, you end with 10 g of stuff — even if it looks completely different.

If a candle burns in air and gets lighter, the gas products (CO₂ and water vapour) escaped into the air. The mass looks lost but really left the container.

In a sealed jar, the mass would not change at all.

mcqs.q: What is the law of conservation of mass?
options: Mass of reactants equals mass of products

mcqs.q: Why does a burning candle appear to lose mass?
options: Gas products escape into the air

numericals.q: If 4 g of magnesium reacts fully with 3 g of oxygen, what mass of magnesium oxide forms (in g)?
